brief:
# Gizmo voice in AmberX: make it work (URGENT)

Brett: Gizmo inside AmberX won't turn on / isn't listening.

1. Read /root/axf-builds/gizmo-voice (branch claude/gizmo-voice, stopped at s2 of 3, 11h ago) and its log; bring its committed/uncommitted work over. Orchestrator ids: `gizmo-voice` (s3 pending) and `amberx-voice-echo-fix` (0/3) — get their briefs: `node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs brief <id>`.
2. Find why Gizmo doesn't start/listen in AmberX (apps/amberx-droid: companion plugin, WatchService, MicGuard, speech, permissions). Fix it end to end: tap/wake → mic on → transcript → Gizmo replies (voice). Fix the echo (Gizmo hearing itself).
3. Tests for the path; build the APK if the repo's CI/scripts do; note how Brett installs it.
4. Mark both orchestrator builds' steps done; add to Shipped features.

Progress: append `<time> START|DONE <step>` to PROGRESS.md here at each step; don't stop between steps. Commit, don't push. Shipped quality, no hard-coded styling.

steps.text: Foreground service keeps talk mode + speech running with the screen off / app backgrounded (AmberX native)
Wire companion talk.ts to the service; transcript shown in the chat; stop from the notification
APK build via CI, phone test of hands-free + interrupt, report

tests.name: npx -y tsx apps/amberx-droid/test.mjs: 2259 → **2316** checks, all green. New: own replies never parse (11) and real commands still do (6); a replay of "Note saved to Inbox." into the listener 12 times, in and past the echo window, still leaves one note; the conversation echo bar; the judge (8 cases
FocusRulesTest (JUnit, 4) run in a JDK 17 container; ListenerRulesTest etc. unchanged. tsc --noEmit clean.
Not run here: Gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug (no Android SDK on the VPS; CI's AmberX job builds and tests it).

open: The focus fix can't be proven on a phone from here: the evidence is the code path (Google's recognizer requesting transient focus) and the tests of the rule. If talk mode still pauses, Settings → Plugins → Listeners shows the reason on the `talk` row.
An echo mis-heard badly enough to score under 0.75 and arriving more than 1.5 s after Gizmo stops still reaches him as a message (rare: his TTS voice is clear).
